#!/bin/bash set -e  # Exit on any error  # Create timestamped log file LOG_FILE="mosaic_install_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log" exec > >(tee -a "$LOG_FILE") exec 2>&1  echo "======================================" echo "MOSAIC VM Setup Script" echo "======================================" echo "Logging to: $LOG_FILE" echo ""  # Check OS version OS_VERSION=$(lsb_release -rs 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown") OS_CODENAME=$(lsb_release -cs 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown") echo "Detected OS: Ubuntu $OS_VERSION ($OS_CODENAME)"  if [ "$OS_VERSION" != "20.04" ]; then   echo "WARNING: This script is optimized for Ubuntu 20.04"   echo "You are running Ubuntu $OS_VERSION - installation may encounter issues"   echo "Press Ctrl+C to cancel, or wait 5 seconds to continue..."   sleep 5 fi echo ""  # Clean up previous failed installations echo "[0/7] Cleaning up previous installation attempts..." rm -rf ~/.local/share/r-miniconda 2>/dev/null || true rm -rf ~/.virtualenvs 2>/dev/null || true rm -rf ~/.conda 2>/dev/null || true sudo rm -rf /root/.local/share/r-miniconda 2>/dev/null || true sudo rm -rf /root/.virtualenvs 2>/dev/null || true echo "Cleanup complete" echo ""  # Update system echo "[1/7] Updating system packages..." sudo apt-get update sudo apt-get upgrade -y  # Install essential build tools echo "[2/7] Installing essential build tools..." sudo apt-get install -y \   git \   ca-certificates \   build-essential \   gfortran \   cmake  # Install R and dependencies echo "[3/7] Installing R (>= 4.1.1)..." sudo apt-get install -y software-properties-common dirmngr wget -qO- https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu/marutter_pubkey.asc | sudo tee -a /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/cran_ubuntu_key.asc sudo add-apt-repository "deb https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu $(lsb_release -cs)-cran40/" sudo apt-get update sudo apt-get install -y r-base r-base-dev  # Install system dependencies for geospatial operations and R packages echo "[4/7] Installing system libraries (GDAL, PROJ, GEOS, HDF5)..." sudo apt-get install -y \   gdal-bin libgdal-dev \   libproj-dev proj-bin \   libgeos-dev libgeos++-dev \   libudunits2-dev \   libcurl4-openssl-dev \   libssl-dev \   libxml2-dev \   libfontconfig1-dev \   libharfbuzz-dev \   libfribidi-dev \   libfreetype6-dev \   libpng-dev \   libtiff5-dev \   libjpeg-dev \   libhdf5-dev \   zlib1g-dev  # Note: cmake (installed above) allows s2 R package to build Abseil from source # Note: libarrow-dev removed - arrow R package will compile from source # This takes longer but avoids repository configuration issues  # Install Python 3.9+ echo "[5/7] Installing Python 3.9+..." sudo apt-get install -y \   python3 \   python3-pip \   python3-venv \   python3-dev  # Verify Python version PYTHON_VERSION=$(python3 --version 2>&1 | grep -oP '\d+\.\d+' | head -1) PYTHON_MAJOR=$(echo $PYTHON_VERSION | cut -d. -f1) PYTHON_MINOR=$(echo $PYTHON_VERSION | cut -d. -f2)  if [ "$PYTHON_MAJOR" -lt 3 ] || ([ "$PYTHON_MAJOR" -eq 3 ] && [ "$PYTHON_MINOR" -lt 9 ]); then   echo "WARNING: Python $PYTHON_VERSION detected, but >= 3.9 required"   echo "Attempting to install Python 3.9..."   sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:deadsnakes/ppa   sudo apt-get update   sudo apt-get install -y python3.9 python3.9-venv python3.9-dev   sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python3 python3 /usr/bin/python3.9 1   echo "Python 3.9 installed and set as default" else   echo "Python $PYTHON_VERSION detected (OK)" fi  # Install critical geospatial R packages first (these often fail) echo "[6/7] Installing critical geospatial R packages..." sudo Rscript -e " options(repos = c(CRAN = 'https://cloud.r-project.org'))  # Install remotes if (!requireNamespace('remotes', quietly = TRUE)) {   install.packages('remotes') }  # Install geospatial packages one by one with error checking cat('Installing sf...
') if (!requireNamespace('sf', quietly = TRUE)) {   install.packages('sf', configure.args = '--with-proj-lib=/usr/lib')   if (!requireNamespace('sf', quietly = TRUE)) {     stop('Failed to install sf package')   } }  cat('Installing terra (version compatible with GEOS 3.8)...
') if (!requireNamespace('terra', quietly = TRUE)) {   # Ubuntu 20.04 has GEOS 3.8, but current terra requires GEOS 3.10+   # Install terra 1.7-71 (last version compatible with GEOS 3.8)   remotes::install_version('terra', version = '1.7.71', repos = 'https://cloud.r-project.org')   if (!requireNamespace('terra', quietly = TRUE)) {     stop('Failed to install terra package')   } }  cat('Installing raster (version compatible with terra 1.7-71)...
') if (!requireNamespace('raster', quietly = TRUE)) {   # Latest raster requires terra >= 1.8.5, but we have terra 1.7-71   # Install raster 3.6-26 (compatible with terra 1.7-71)   remotes::install_version('raster', version = '3.6.26', repos = 'https://cloud.r-project.org')   if (!requireNamespace('raster', quietly = TRUE)) {     stop('Failed to install raster package')   } }  cat('Geospatial packages installed successfully
') "  # Now install MOSAIC with all dependencies echo "[7/7] Installing MOSAIC R package..." sudo Rscript -e "options(repos = c(CRAN = 'https://cloud.r-project.org')); \   remotes::install_github('InstituteforDiseaseModeling/MOSAIC-pkg', dependencies = TRUE, upgrade = 'never')"  # Install Python dependencies (run as user, not root) echo "[7/7] Installing Python dependencies..." Rscript -e "MOSAIC::install_dependencies(force = TRUE)"  # Configure R wrapper for Ubuntu 20.04 GLIBCXX compatibility echo "Configuring R wrapper for Ubuntu 20.04 compatibility..." if [ "$OS_VERSION" = "20.04" ]; then   echo "  Creating r-mosaic-R and r-mosaic-Rscript wrappers..."    # Create ~/bin directory   mkdir -p ~/bin    # Create R wrapper script with auto-detection of libstdc++ location   cat > ~/bin/r-mosaic-R <<'EOF' #!/usr/bin/env bash # Find a modern libstdc++ inside common reticulate env locations candidates=(   "$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/lib/libstdc++.so.6"   "$HOME/.local/share/r-miniconda/envs/r-mosaic/lib/libstdc++.so.6"   "$HOME/.local/share/r-miniconda/envs/r-reticulate/lib/libstdc++.so.6" ) for f in "${candidates[@]}"; do   if [ -f "$f" ] && strings "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "GLIBCXX_3\.4\.29"; then     export LD_PRELOAD="$f${LD_PRELOAD:+:$LD_PRELOAD}"     export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(dirname "$f")${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"     break   fi done # Preload libexpat from conda environment to avoid system's old version if [ -f "$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/lib/libexpat.so.1" ]; then   export LD_PRELOAD="$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/lib/libexpat.so.1${LD_PRELOAD:+:$LD_PRELOAD}" fi # Set R library path to include user library export R_LIBS_USER="$HOME/R/library" # If we later want to hard-pin Python for reticulate: [ -x "$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/bin/python" ] && export RETICULATE_PYTHON="$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/bin/python" exec R "$@" EOF   chmod +x ~/bin/r-mosaic-R   # Shebang guard: a corrupted (indented) shebang makes the kernel fall back to   # /bin/sh (dash), which dies on the bash array with `Syntax error: "(" unexpected`.   head -1 ~/bin/r-mosaic-R | grep -q '^#!' || { echo "ERROR: ~/bin/r-mosaic-R shebang malformed (not at column 0)"; exit 1; }    # Create Rscript wrapper with same logic   cat > ~/bin/r-mosaic-Rscript <<'EOF' #!/usr/bin/env bash # Same preload logic for Rscript candidates=(   "$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/lib/libstdc++.so.6"   "$HOME/.local/share/r-miniconda/envs/r-mosaic/lib/libstdc++.so.6"   "$HOME/.local/share/r-miniconda/envs/r-reticulate/lib/libstdc++.so.6" ) for f in "${candidates[@]}"; do   if [ -f "$f" ] && strings "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "GLIBCXX_3\.4\.29"; then     export LD_PRELOAD="$f${LD_PRELOAD:+:$LD_PRELOAD}"     export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(dirname "$f")${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"     break   fi done # Preload libexpat from conda environment to avoid system's old version if [ -f "$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/lib/libexpat.so.1" ]; then   export LD_PRELOAD="$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/lib/libexpat.so.1${LD_PRELOAD:+:$LD_PRELOAD}" fi # Set R library path to include user library export R_LIBS_USER="$HOME/R/library" [ -x "$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/bin/python" ] && export RETICULATE_PYTHON="$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/bin/python" exec Rscript "$@" EOF   chmod +x ~/bin/r-mosaic-Rscript   head -1 ~/bin/r-mosaic-Rscript | grep -q '^#!' || { echo "ERROR: ~/bin/r-mosaic-Rscript shebang malformed (not at column 0)"; exit 1; }    # Ensure launchers are first on PATH for this session and future shells   export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"   if ! grep -q 'export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"' ~/.bashrc; then     echo 'export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc   fi    echo "  ✓ Created r-mosaic-R wrapper at ~/bin/r-mosaic-R"   echo "  ✓ Created r-mosaic-Rscript wrapper at ~/bin/r-mosaic-Rscript"   echo "  ✓ Added ~/bin to PATH in ~/.bashrc" else   echo "  Skipping wrapper creation (only needed for Ubuntu 20.04)" fi  # Verify installation echo "" echo "Verifying installation..." Rscript -e "   library(MOSAIC)   result <- tryCatch({     MOSAIC::check_dependencies()     TRUE   }, error = function(e) {     cat('ERROR:', e\$message, '
')     FALSE   })   if (!result) quit(status = 1) "  if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then   echo ""   echo "======================================"   echo "Installation complete and verified!"   echo "======================================"   echo ""   echo "Installation Summary:"   echo "  - R version: $(R --version | head -1)"   echo "  - Python version: $(python3 --version)"   echo "  - MOSAIC R package: $(Rscript -e "cat(as.character(packageVersion('MOSAIC')))" 2>/dev/null)"   echo "  - Python environment: ~/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic"   echo "  - Conda location: ~/.local/share/r-miniconda"   echo ""   echo "Next steps:"   echo "  1. Test MOSAIC: Rscript -e 'library(MOSAIC); MOSAIC::check_dependencies()'"   echo "  2. View documentation: https://institutefordiseasemodeling.github.io/MOSAIC-pkg/"   echo "  3. Report issues: https://github.com/InstituteforDiseaseModeling/MOSAIC-pkg/issues"   echo ""   echo "Full installation log saved to: $LOG_FILE" else   echo ""   echo "======================================"   echo "Installation completed with errors"   echo "======================================"   echo ""   echo "Please check the error messages above and try the following:"   echo "  1. Review the full log: cat $LOG_FILE"   echo "  2. Check system requirements: Ubuntu 20.04, 8GB RAM, 20GB disk"   echo "  3. Re-run this script (it will clean up previous attempts)"   echo "  4. Report issues: https://github.com/InstituteforDiseaseModeling/MOSAIC-pkg/issues"   echo ""   echo "Full installation log saved to: $LOG_FILE"   exit 1 fi

what: Run a fixed number of simulations for one location
title: Running MOSAIC
code: # Load required packages library(MOSAIC)   # Create output directory and set up logging dir_output <- path.expand("~/MOSAIC/output/ETH_fixed") if (!dir.exists(dir_output)) dir.create(dir_output, recursive = TRUE)  set_root_directory("~/MOSAIC")   priors_ETH <- get_location_priors(iso="ETH") config_ETH <- get_location_config(iso="ETH")  control_ETH <- mosaic_control_defaults()  control_ETH$calibration$n_simulations <- 500 control_ETH$calibration$n_iterations <- 2  control_ETH$parallel$enable <- TRUE control_ETH$parallel$n_cores <- parallel::detectCores()-1  control_ETH$targets$ESS_param <- 100 control_ETH$targets$ESS_param_prop <- 0.9 control_ETH$targets$ESS_best <- 50 control_ETH$targets$ESS_method <- 'perplexity'  control_ETH$sampling$sample_tau_i <- FALSE # Travel probability control_ETH$sampling$sample_mobility_gamma <- FALSE   # Gravity model exponent control_ETH$sampling$sample_mobility_omega <- FALSE   # Mobility rate  control_ETH$likelihood$weight_cases <- 1 control_ETH$likelihood$weight_deaths <- 0.05  control_ETH$predictions$n_iter_best <- 30 control_ETH$predictions$n_iter_ensemble <- 5   control_ETH$paths$clean_output <- TRUE control_ETH$io <- mosaic_io_presets("fast")  result_ETH <- run_MOSAIC(      dir_output = dir_output,      config = config_ETH,      priors = priors_ETH,      control = control_ETH,      resume = FALSE )

title: Running MOSAIC
code: # Load required packages library(MOSAIC)  # Create output directory and set up logging dir_output <- path.expand("~/MOSAIC/output/ETH_KEN") if (!dir.exists(dir_output)) dir.create(dir_output, recursive = TRUE)  set_root_directory("~/MOSAIC")  iso_codes <- c("ETH", "KEN")  priors <- get_location_priors(iso=iso_codes) config <- get_location_config(iso=iso_codes)  control <- mosaic_control_defaults()  control$calibration$n_simulations <- 'auto' control$calibration$n_iterations <- 3 control$calibration$batch_size_adaptive <- 500 control$calibration$min_batches_adaptive <- 5 control$calibration$max_batches_adaptive <- 10 control$calibration$target_r2_adaptive <- 0.95 control$calibration$max_simulations_total <- 1e+06  control$parallel$enable <- TRUE control$parallel$n_cores <- parallel::detectCores()-1  control$targets$ESS_param <- 100 control$targets$ESS_param_prop <- 0.95 control$targets$ESS_best <- 30 control$targets$ESS_method <- 'perplexity'  control$sampling$sample_tau_i <- length(iso_codes) > 1 # Travel probability control$sampling$sample_mobility_gamma <- length(iso_codes) > 1  # Gravity model exponent control$sampling$sample_mobility_omega <- length(iso_codes) > 1  # Mobility rate  control$likelihood$weight_cases <- 1 control$likelihood$weight_deaths <- 0.05  control$predictions$n_iter_best <- 50 control$predictions$n_iter_ensemble <- 10  control$paths$clean_output <- TRUE control$io <- mosaic_io_presets("fast")  control$logging$verbose <- TRUE  result <- run_MOSAIC(      dir_output = dir_output,      config = config,      priors = priors,      control = control,      resume = FALSE )

title: Running simulations
text: MOSAIC includes pre-configured parameter sets different transmission scenarios. Let’s run visualize two key scenarios: epidemic endemic transmission.

title: Running simulations
text: epidemic configuration simulates outbreak dynamics explosive growth patterns typical cholera epidemics.
code:
library(MOSAIC)  # Run epidemic scenario config <- MOSAIC::config_simulation_epidemic  model_epidemic <- run_simulation(config = config, seed = 123, quiet = FALSE)  # Extract time series results (locations x time matrices) cases_epidemic <- as.matrix(model_epidemic$results$reported_cases) deaths_epidemic <- as.matrix(model_epidemic$results$reported_deaths)  # Get metadata locations <- config_simulation_epidemic$location_name n_locations <- length(locations) n_timesteps <- ncol(cases_epidemic)  # Calculate total burden total_cases_epidemic <- sum(cases_epidemic, na.rm = TRUE) total_deaths_epidemic <- sum(deaths_epidemic, na.rm = TRUE)  cat(sprintf("Epidemic Scenario Results:
")) cat(sprintf("  Total cases: %s
", format(total_cases_epidemic, big.mark = ","))) cat(sprintf("  Total deaths: %s
", format(total_deaths_epidemic, big.mark = ","))) cat(sprintf("  Locations: %d
", n_locations)) cat(sprintf("  Time steps: %d
", n_timesteps))  # Plot epidemic time series by location png("figures/running_mosaic_epidemic.png", width = 800, height = 600, res = 120)  colors <- c("#009ADE", "#FF1F5B", "#00CD6C")  # Blue, Pink, Green par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(3, 4, 3, 1), oma = c(2, 0, 0, 0))  matplot(t(cases_epidemic), type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2, col = colors,         xlab = "", ylab = "Reported Cases",         main = "Epidemic Transmission Simulation")  matplot(t(deaths_epidemic), type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2, col = colors,         xlab = "Time step", ylab = "Reported Deaths", main = "")  par(fig = c(0, 1, 0, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), new = TRUE) plot(0, 0, type = "n", bty = "n", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n") legend("bottom", legend = locations, col = colors, lty = 1, lwd = 2,        horiz = TRUE, bty = "n", xpd = TRUE)  dev.off() cat("Saved: figures/running_mosaic_epidemic.png
")

Param ESS: pass=1.0 (100%), warn=0.8 (80%) subset percentile (percentile_used target_max_best_subset / n_total * 100) carries information B_size_upper denominator, status reported summary$percentile_status gated. function defaults targets (300 / 0.95 / 0.5) run_MOSAIC() control defaults (ESS_best = 100, A_best = 0.70, CVw_best = 1.0); run_MOSAIC() always passes targets explicitly.

title: Calculate Kullback-Leibler Divergence Between Two Distributions — calc_kl_divergence
text: KL divergence KL(P||Q) calculated : $$KL(P||Q) = \int p(x) \log(p(x) / q(x)) dx$$ P represents distribution samples1 Q represents distribution samples2. densities weighted kernel density estimates whose bandwidths use weighted Silverman rule Kish effective sample size \(n_{eff} = (\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\), concentrated weight vector yields narrow density even draws spread (equal weights stats::bw.nrd0()). integral \(\int p \log(p/q)\) evaluated trapezoidal rule grid support P (integrand non-zero), Q interpolated full-range KDE, value level log(n_points) P much narrower Q. v0.100.0 densities used unweighted bandwidths one grid pooled range densities renormalised discrete probabilities, narrow P saturated near log(n_points). Note KL divergence symmetric: KL(P||Q) != KL(Q||P).

title: Calculate Kullback-Leibler Divergence Between Two Distributions — calc_kl_divergence
code: # Example 1: Compare two normal distributions set.seed(123) samples1 <- rnorm(1000, mean = 0, sd = 1) samples2 <- rnorm(1000, mean = 0.5, sd = 1.2) kl_div <- calc_kl_divergence(samples1, NULL, samples2, NULL) print(paste("KL divergence:", round(kl_div, 4))) #> [1] "KL divergence: 0.1353"  # Example 2: Using weighted samples samples1 <- rnorm(500) weights1 <- runif(500, 0.5, 1.5) samples2 <- rnorm(500, mean = 1) weights2 <- runif(500, 0.5, 1.5) kl_div_weighted <- calc_kl_divergence(samples1, weights1, samples2, weights2)  # Example 3: Comparing posterior to prior in Bayesian analysis # prior_samples <- rnorm(1000, mean = 0, sd = 2)  # Prior # posterior_samples <- rnorm(1000, mean = 1, sd = 0.5)  # Posterior # kl_div <- calc_kl_divergence(posterior_samples, NULL, prior_samples, NULL)

what: Deaths log-likelihood with the reported CFR integrated out — calc_log_likelihood_deaths_integrated
title: Deaths log-likelihood with the reported CFR integrated out — calc_log_likelihood_deaths_integrated
text: Scores observed deaths simulated path reported case fatality ratio (CFR) integrated analytically. Given path, expected reported deaths day CFR times known exposure, CFR's level can solved per path rather sampled. CFR modelled time-varying prior mu_jt shifted logit scale location-level offset one level per calendar year: $$\mathrm{logit}\,\mu_{jt} = \mathrm{logit}\,\mu^{0}_{jt} + a_j +   \sum_y B_y(t)\,\delta_{j,y},\qquad a_j \sim N(0, s_j^2),\quad   \delta_{j,y} \sim N(0, \sigma_y^2)\ (y \le y^*_j),\quad   \delta_{j,y} \sim N(f_j, \sigma_y^2)\ (y > y^*_j),$$ \(B_y(t)\) 1 inside calendar year \(y\) blends linearly next year 60 days centred 1 January, CFR step year boundary. year's deviation LEVEL year: year observed part fitted months observed applied unchanged rest year (interpolated basis extrapolate within-year trend past data instead). \(y^*_j\) latest year observed past New Year blend (year last scored day minus 30 days), later year forecast year centred forecast shift \(f_j\) usual year--year spread \(\sigma_y\). run_MOSAIC() sets \(f_j\) posterior ensemble's mean deviation \(y^*_j\), forecast continues latest calibrated CFR shift shared members – without member's case error, \(\delta_{j,y^*_j}\) also absorbs – instead reverting prior's long-run level. Deaths aggregated reporting weeks scored quasi-Poisson likelihood: Poisson log-likelihood divided per-location dispersion \(\phi_j\), small additive background week's expected deaths. quasi-Poisson score CFR level Poisson score, given path fitted CFR reproduces observed deaths totals (negative binomial score weight low-count weeks far peak bias level); \(\phi_j\) tempers likelihood deaths scatter Poisson. location offsets fitted Newton's method marginal likelihood Laplace approximation mode.

title: Deaths log-likelihood with the reported CFR integrated out — calc_log_likelihood_deaths_integrated
text: obs_deaths Matrix [locations x days] (vector, one location) observed reported deaths. exposure Matrix shape: expected reported deaths per unit reported CFR day, (rho / chi_epidemic) * onsets onset day. title: Stable log-mean-exp computation — calc_log_mean_exp
text: log-mean-exp vector \(x\) computed : $$ \mathrm{LME}(x) = \max(x) + \log\left(\frac{1}{|x|}\sum_i e^{x_i - \max(x)}\right) $$ numerically stable : maximum value subtracted exponentiation, preventing overflow least one exponentiated term equals 1, preventing underflow Equivalent log(mean(exp(x))) without numerical issues Dropping -Inf instead shrink denominator \(|x|\) bias result upward: averaging one zero-likelihood replicate \(m\) gain \(\log(m/(m-1))\).

title: Stable log-mean-exp computation — calc_log_mean_exp
code: # Basic usage x <- c(-100, -101, -99) calc_log_mean_exp(x)  # -99.69 #> [1] -99.69101  # Compare with the naive form (underflows for very negative values) log(mean(exp(x))) #> [1] -99.69101  # -Inf counts as a zero likelihood; NA is dropped calc_log_mean_exp(c(0, -Inf))        # log(0.5) #> [1] -0.6931472 calc_log_mean_exp(c(-50, -60, NA))   # log-mean-exp of -50 and -60 #> [1] -50.6931  # Empty, all-missing, or all -Inf input calc_log_mean_exp(c())           # NA #> [1] NA calc_log_mean_exp(c(NA, NaN))    # NA #> [1] NA calc_log_mean_exp(c(-Inf, -Inf)) # -Inf #> [1] -Inf

title: Calculate Effective Sample Size (ESS) — calc_model_ess
text: Two methods available: Kish method (method = "kish"): Uses standard Kish ESS formula: \(\mathrm{ESS} = (\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\). provides measure much information retained using weighted samples compared unweighted sample size. Perplexity method (method = "perplexity"): Uses exponential entropy: \(\mathrm{ESS} = \exp(-\sum w_i \log w_i)\), weights first normalized sum 1. measures effective number models based entropy weight distribution. Also known perplexity exponential entropy. methods yield values 1 (weight one model) \(n\) (uniform weights), measure slightly different aspects weight concentration. Kish formula commonly used survey sampling, perplexity common information theory model averaging.

title: Compute Parameter Sensitivity Ranking (R2-HSIC) — calc_model_parameter_sensitivity
text: Computes R2-HSIC (Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion) sampled parameter log-likelihood calibration samples.parquet file. HSIC measures statistical dependence without assuming linearity, monotonicity, independence among inputs, making valid importance-weighted posterior samples parameters correlated (Da Veiga 2015). R2-HSIC index equals zero iff parameter log-likelihood statistically independent (RBF kernel).

text: Converts numeric vector model scores (treated loss-like, .e., lower--better) normalized posterior weights using Gibbs (generalized Bayes) formulation: $$w_m(\eta) = \frac{\exp(-\eta \, x_m)}{\sum_{j=1}^K \exp(-\eta \, x_j)} \,,$$ \(x_m\) loss (information criterion) model \(m\) \(\eta \ge 0\) inverse temperature (sharpness) parameter.

Higher values concentrate weight best models; lower values flatten weights. Typical choices: 0.5 \(\Delta\)AIC (Akaike weights), 1 \(-\log L\). verbose Logical; TRUE, prints brief diagnostics (range x, applied shift, entropy, effective number models). ... title: Gibbs-Posterior Model Weights — calc_model_weights_gibbs
text: function agnostic specific form \(x\); smaller values assumed indicate better models. Common choices include: \(x = \Delta \mathrm{AIC}\) \; (use eta = 1/2 recover Akaike weights), \(x = -\log L\) \; (use eta = 1 normalized likelihood weights), Cross-validated losses (e.g., RMSE, MSLE), proper scoring rule. start higher--better score (e.g., log-likelihood), pass x = -score lower--better holds. Numerical stability: implementation subtracts \(\min(x)\) prior exponentiation; shift leaves normalized weights unchanged helps avoid underflow/overflow. Special cases: eta = 0: uniform weights. eta = Inf: hard selection (ties share weight equally). x equal: uniform weights.

text: Transforms daily suitability series \(\psi_t \[0,1]\) logit-scale affine calibration, optional causal EWMA smoothing, optional time offset \(k\). missing values introduced shift (pre-existing) filled using either LOCF (default) linear interpolation.

title: Calibrate Daily Suitability on the Logit Scale (vector; optional causal EWMA + time offset + NA filling) — calc_psi_star
code: calc_psi_star(   psi,   a = 1,   b = 0,   z = 1,   k = 0,   eps = 1e-06,   fill_method = c("locf", "linear"),   warn_k_rounding = TRUE )

title: Calibrate Daily Suitability on the Logit Scale (vector; optional causal EWMA + time offset + NA filling) — calc_psi_star
text: psi Numeric vector \([0,1]\) (daily suitability \(\psi_t\)). Numeric (>0). Shape/gain logit scale (\(>1\) sharpens; \(<1\) flattens). b Numeric. Scale/offset logit scale (baseline /). z Numeric \((0,1]\) controlling causal EWMA smoothing; 1 = smoothing. k Numeric integer; time offset days. Positive = forward/right; negative = backward/left. Non-integers rounded nearest integer. eps Small positive number clip psi away {0,1} qlogis. fill_method Character; one c("locf","linear") controlling NA gaps filled. warn_k_rounding Logical; TRUE (default), warns k rounded nearest integer. Set FALSE suppress warning.

title: Calibrate Daily Suitability on the Logit Scale (vector; optional causal EWMA + time offset + NA filling) — calc_psi_star
text: Numeric vector \(\tilde\psi^{\star}_t\) (length psi): calibrated, offset, NA-filled, smoothed z<1.

title: Calibrate Daily Suitability on the Logit Scale (vector; optional causal EWMA + time offset + NA filling) — calc_psi_star
text: Offset (index shift, days): \(\psi^{(k)}_t = \psi_{t-k}\). Positive \(k\) shifts series forward/right (delay); negative \(k\) shifts backward/left. Non-integer \(k\) rounded nearest integer. Calibration (odds-space power & scale): $$\psi_t^{\star}=\sigma\!\big(\cdot \mathrm{logit}(\tilde\psi_t)+b\big),\quad \tilde\psi_t=\min\{\max(\psi^{(k)}_t,\varepsilon),\,1-\varepsilon\}$$ \(\text{odds}^\star_t = e^{b}\,(\text{odds}_t)^{}\), \; \(\text{odds}_t=\tilde\psi_t/(1-\tilde\psi_t)\). Optional causal smoothing (look-ahead): $$\tilde\psi^{\star}_t = z\,\psi^{\star}_t + (1-z)\,\tilde\psi^{\star}_{t-1},\quad z\(0,1],\ \tilde\psi^{\star}_1=\psi^{\star}_1.$$ NA filling (calibration, smoothing): Choose via fill_method: "locf" — forward fill (LOCF) backward pass leading gaps. "linear" — linear interpolation interior gaps constant edge extension. values NA shifting, function falls back constant baseline \(\sigma(b)\).

title: Calibrate Daily Suitability on the Logit Scale (vector; optional causal EWMA + time offset + NA filling) — calc_psi_star
code: # Basic usage with integer k (no warnings) psi <- c(0.1, 0.3, 0.7, 0.9, 0.5) result1 <- calc_psi_star(psi, a = 1.2, b = 0.5, k = 2)  # Non-integer k with warning (default behavior) result2 <- calc_psi_star(psi, a = 1.2, b = 0.5, k = 2.744) #> Warning: `k` (2.744) is not an integer; rounding to 3.  # Non-integer k without warning result3 <- calc_psi_star(psi, a = 1.2, b = 0.5, k = 2.744, warn_k_rounding = FALSE)  # With EWMA smoothing result4 <- calc_psi_star(psi, a = 1.2, b = 0.5, k = 2, z = 0.8)

title: Calculate spatial importation hazard — calc_spatial_hazard
text: Computes daily probability least one new infection introduced destination location j day t using gravity‐style coupling infectious prevalence across locations.  formulation adapted Bjørnstad & Grenfell (2008) () folds gravity weights directly prevalence term instead using separate coupling constant, (ii) uses location-specific departure probability tau (\(\tau_j\), daily probability resident \(j\) travels outside home location; see "Spatial dynamics" MOSAIC model description) split population stay--home share \(1-\tau_j\) travelling share \(\tau_j\). Concretely, time t destination j hazard $$\mathcal H_{jt} \,=\, \frac{\beta_{jt}\,S^{\*}_{jt}        \bigl[1-\exp\{-(S^{\*}_{jt}/N_{jt})\,\bar y_{jt}\}\bigr]}       {1+\beta_{jt}\,S^{\*}_{jt}},$$ \(S^{\*}_{jt} = (1-\tau_j)\bigl(S_{jt}+V^{\mathrm{sus}}_{1,jt}+V^{\mathrm{sus}}_{2,jt}\bigr)\) stay--home susceptible pool. \(\bar y_{jt}\) gravity‑weighted prevalence infection entire metapopulation (including destination): $$\bar y_{jt} = \frac{ (1-\tau_j)(I_{1,jt}+I_{2,jt}) +         \sum_{\neq j}\tau_i\,\pi_{ij}\,(I_{1,}+I_{2,}) }        {\sum_{k} N_{kt} }.$$ Note: specification differs two‑stage form original paper used later work mobility matrix carries full coupling strength.

title: Combine WHO and GTFCC Vaccination Data — combine_vaccination_data
text: function performs intelligent campaign matching using following approach: Load Processed Data: - Reads GTFCC processed vaccination data files Intelligent Matching: - Matches campaigns country, approximate date (within tolerance), dose similarity - Uses multiple passes different tolerance levels maximize accurate matching - Identifies truly unique campaigns present GTFCC Data Combination: - Prioritizes GTFCC data (marked source = "GTFCC") - Adds unique campaigns (marked source = "WHO_only") - Includes campaigns present (marked source = "GTFCC_WHO_matched") - match_confidence "high" (Step 1: +/-7 days, +/-5% doses), "medium" (Step 2: within tolerances), "low" (Step 3: +/-30 days, dose, Step 4 ), "GTFCC_only" / "WHO_only" - Steps 1-3 GTFCC campaign absorbs one campaign, genuinely separate second campaign within 30 days kept - GTFCC records campaign row's ICG request number, request's campaign(s) candidates every step - Step 4 (ICG request): GTFCC rows per-request totals (deliveries summed) rows per shipment, still-unmatched shipment absorbed GTFCC campaign ICG request number (20174 = GTFCC 201704) long doses assigned campaign stay within (1 + dose_tolerance) GTFCC doses (e.g. MOZ 2017-I04: 709.1K GTFCC vs 329.6K + 354.6K ); row whose request number GTFCC use matched ICG decision date (+/-7 days) within dose tolerance instead - Step 5 (repeated -rows): -rows sharing country, ICG request decision date kept campaign-date order summed doses stay within (1 + dose_tolerance) request's approved total; rows dropped duplicate listings (MWI 20182: two 500,600-dose rows 500,600 approved) - GTFCC request columns (req_id, delivery_schedule, round_sequence, round_basis; see process_GTFCC_vaccination_data) carried every GTFCC row, matched . -rows delivery schedule round information (round_basis = "unknown"), est_vaccination_rate releases doses campaign date counts first doses. Quality Assurance: - Validates data structure matches downstream requirements - Ensures required columns present - Maintains date ID formatting standards

text: Empirical-Bayes shrinkage style DESeq2 (Love, Huber & Anders 2014): \(\log k_j \sim N(\log k_{trend}(\mu_j), \sigma_p^2)\). location's estimate weighted PRECISION, \(w_j = \sigma_p^2 / (\sigma_p^2 + s_j^2)\) \(s_j = se_j / k_j\) (delta method), prior variance recovered DESeq2 variance decomposition \(\sigma_p^2 = Var(resid) - \overline{s_j^2}\). flat blend posterior mean sampling variance equalled prior variance. title: Cholera Epidemic Peaks Data — epidemic_peaks
text: Scope: dataset full historical detection record surveillance time series (years combined daily series, observed weeks – AI Fourier reconstructions excluded) pre-trimmed particular simulation window. Consumers score peaks specific config window (e.g. calc_model_likelihood(), Python likelihood port, simulation config builders) must filter [date_start, date_stop] first – otherwise .min(abs(date_seq - peak_date)) silently snaps --window peaks t=1 t=N biases peak-shape likelihood terms. internal helper MOSAIC:::.filter_epidemic_peaks() canonical filter applied build time inside make_config_default.R, runtime inside get_location_config(), defensively inside calc_model_likelihood(). Epidemic peaks identified using following methodology: Time series smoothing 28-day running mean window Local maxima detection 10-day comparison windows Prominence-based filtering (minimum 8% maximum smoothed value countries; country-specific overrides ) Minimum peak height threshold 3 smoothed cases (default) Minimum 75-day separation consecutive peaks Peak boundaries defined incidence drops 1/3 peak height Country-specific adjustments applied : Niger (NER): Lower prominence threshold (1.5%) gradual peaks Cameroon (CMR): Adjusted threshold (4%) plateau-shaped peaks Ethiopia (ETH): Lower threshold (3%) multiple outbreaks Detected peaks sit observed weeks: imputed (AI Fourier, assumed-zero) weeks treated missing (multi-week report spread window counts observed), peak day must observed cases > 0, detected peak whose window least half imputed days dropped. manual corrections documented outbreaks exempt window filter. Manual corrections applied known issues including: Ethiopia 2024: February peak corrected March (sustained outbreak) DRC 2023: Added January peak (filtered due proximity) Nigeria 2024: Added October peak Kenya 2022-2023: Added December 2022, removed June 2023 minor peak Mozambique: Added February 2024 March 2025 peaks Somalia: Added major April 2017 peak 2024-2025 peaks Zambia: Added January 2018 peak Tanzania: Added January 2017 peak

text: function assembles literature table ID50 estimates spanning direct human-volunteer challenge studies (Hornick 1971, Cash 1974, Levine 1981/1988, Tacket 1999), QMRA Beta-Poisson fits (Haas, Rose & Gerba 1999), expert-review summaries (Nelson et al. 2009, Kaper et al. 1995), values adopted convention cholera modelling literature (Codeco 2001, Hartley et al. 2006). source weighted relevance endemic / buffered exposure context relevant sub-Saharan African transmission settings. lognormal fit weighted maximum-likelihood log10 scale. MOSAIC dose-response follows Codeco (2001) Hartley et al. (2006): infection hazard saturating Michaelis-Menten function environmental concentration half-saturation \(\kappa\). Historical cholera models fixed \(\kappa = 10^6\) cells, value traceable Sack (1971) Hornick et al. (1971) unbuffered water-exposure healthy adults. Modern re-analyses buffered-exposure volunteer studies (NaHCO3 neutralisation, representative typical endemic exposure food contaminated drinking water) consistently support lower central estimate \(\sim 10^5\) CFU, substantial -study heterogeneity. Fitting: source contributes point estimate \(\log_{10} \kappa_i\) weight \(w_i\) reflecting evidentiary quality. weighted mean standard deviation log10 scale converted directly lognormal meanlog sdlog (meanlog = mu_log10 * ln 10, sdlog = sd_log10 * ln 10); refit applied.

text: Compiles meta-analysis published Vibrio cholerae shedding anchors (stool concentration x time-averaged daily stool volume) symptomatic infections fits lognormal prior per-person-per-day shedding rate used MOSAIC environmental reservoir update: $$W(t+1) \mathrel{+}= (1 - \theta_j) \cdot \mathrm{Poisson}(\zeta_1 \cdot I_{\mathrm{sym}})$$ \(\zeta_1\) expected total V. cholerae cells shed per symptomatic infected person per day shedding phase. \(\gamma_1\) parameter handles shedding-phase duration; \(\zeta_1\) daily rate, total-per-infection.

title: Estimate Prior Distribution for Symptomatic Shedding Rate (zeta_1) — est_zeta_1_prior
text: function assembles literature table per-person-per-day shedding anchors constructed stool concentration (\(c\), cells per mL) times time-averaged daily stool volume (\(V\), mL per day) defined severity classes (severe, moderate, mild). weighted lognormal fit maximum-likelihood log10 scale. severity-weighted pool row also built severity_mix argument, shown forest plot (weight 0; see Details). Assembly equation. literature entry contributes \(\zeta_{1,} = c_i \times V_i\) lower upper bounds taken spread concentration volume anchors severity class. Time-averaged stool volumes used (V_sev = 4, V_mod = 2, V_mild = 0.3 L/day, lowered v0.29.1 8 / 4 / 0.5 average 1-2 week clinical course) engine's Poisson update multiplies rate current I_sym compartment, already integrates shedding course via \(\gamma_1\). Peak purging rates (~1 L/h, ~14-24 L/day) treated upper-bound sensitivity rows, central anchor. Severity-weighted pool rows. pool rows (endemic mix severity_mix, fixed outbreak mix 0.35 / 0.40 / 0.25) derived severe, moderate mild class rows, since v0.29.1 carry weight 0: fitting well count severe class three times. severity_mix therefore changes pool row shown forest plot fitted prior. default mix severe class ~91 percent pool (\(0.2 \times 4 \times 10^{11}\) \(0.4 \times 2 \times 10^{10} + 0.4 \times 3 \times 10^{7}\)), \(c_{\mathrm{sev}} = 10^8\) 1000x \(c_{\mathrm{mild}} = 10^5\) cells/mL. Weighted MLE log10 scale. Weighted mean SD log10 scale converted lognormal meanlog sdlog: $$\mu_{\log_{10}} = \frac{\sum w_i \log_{10}(\zeta_{1,})}{\sum w_i}, \quad       \sigma^2_{\log_{10}} = \frac{\sum w_i (\log_{10}(\zeta_{1,}) - \mu_{\log_{10}})^2}{\sum w_i}$$ meanlog = mu_log10 * ln(10) sdlog = sigma_log10 * ln(10). Sensitivity returns. $sensitivity list contains three alternative fits: include_calib (refits MOSAIC calibration posterior row weight 0.25, producing much wider sdlog Frame-B-calibrated value 7 OOM biological-units literature anchors), volume_peak (rescales severe-class V = 4 L/day rows V = 10 L/day), volume_low (rescales V = 1.5 L/day). Per-day vs per-infection. zeta_1 per-day shedding rate symptomatic infectious period; \(\gamma_1^{-1}\) (~10 d) governs duration. cumulative cells shed per symptomatic infection therefore approximately zeta_1 / gamma_1, per-infection contribution ratio vs asymptomatic zeta_ratio * (gamma_2 / gamma_1) (~5x per-day ratio current gamma priors). comparing prior literature quotes cumulative stool output per infection, apply duration multiplier. Relation documented priors. Earlier MOSAIC-docs narrative states zeta_1 ~ Uniform(10^4, 10^8). range derives Frame-B calibration rescaling superseded lognormal literature-derived prior. new prior's 95% CI extends ~10^13, well stale Uniform upper bound. Primary source notes stored claude/zeta_priors_update/zeta_sources/ (14 PDFs + 32 source notes). See claude/zeta_priors_update/plan_zeta_priors_implementation.md full provenance.

title: Estimate Prior Distribution for Asymptomatic Shedding Rate (zeta_2) — est_zeta_2_prior
text: function assembles small literature table per-person-per-day asymptomatic shedding anchors. evidence base thin: Nelson 2009 gives verbatim primary-source anchor ("approximately 10^3 vibrios per gram stool") Kaper 1995 provides expert-review range (10^3 10^5 cells per gram). Given single primary source, fit applies hard floor sdlog >= 2.0 honestly reflect \(n_{\mathrm{independent}} = 1\). Assembly equation. entry contributes \(\zeta_{2,} = c_i \times V_i\) V = 150 g/day taken normal adult physiology (100-250 g/day); cholera-specific asymptomatic stool-volume measurement exists. Single-source caveat sdlog floor. central anchor rests single primary source (Nelson 2009). fit applies hard floor sdlog >= 2.0 (raised 1.5 rev 1 per modeller review). floor preserves lognormal median (meanlog unchanged); mode shifts left consequence. weights 1.0 / 0.1 / 0.1 (v0.29.1) weighted log10 mean ~5.34, median ~2.2e5; sdlog = 2.0 95 percent CI spans roughly 4.4e3 1.1e7 - factor ~50 side - correct spread cover +/- 1 order--magnitude error single primary source. King 2008 caveat (documentation ). King, Ionides, Pascual & Bouma (2008) describe "negligible quantity vibrio" shed asymptomatic hosts natural-vaccination model. qualitative directionally supports small zeta_2 / large zeta_ratio, give quantitative value. therefore included fitted row - treating qualitative claim quantitative data masquerade ignorance evidence. See claude/zeta_priors_update/zeta_sources/12_King_2008_Nature_inapparent.md. Leave-Nelson-sensitivity. $sensitivity$leave_nelson_out returns fit using Kaper review rows. fit effective n_primary_sources = 0 (Kaper review cites Nelson-era primary data) published warning, usable prior. n_sources caveat. returned $fit$n_sources equals nrow(fit_df) = 3 (Nelson, Kaper-lower, Kaper-upper). effective number independent primary sources 1 (Nelson 2009); Kaper 1995 review contribute independent primary data. sdlog-floor mechanism encodes single-source risk regardless n_sources count. Per-day vs per-infection. zeta_2 per-day shedding rate asymptomatic infection; \(\gamma_2^{-1}\) (~2 d) governs duration. Nelson's verbatim claim asymptomatic shedding lasts "one day" – close current gamma_2 prior. Cumulative cells per asymptomatic infection zeta_2 / gamma_2. Relation documented priors. Earlier MOSAIC-docs narrative states zeta_2 ~ Uniform(0.01, 10^3). range derives Frame-B calibration rescaling superseded lognormal literature-derived prior, whose 95% CI extends ~10^7.

text: function produces THREE candidate lognormal fits. direct channel () shipped prior: returned $fit, written param_zeta_ratio_prior.csv, stored data-raw/make_priors_default.R priors_default$parameters_global$zeta_ratio. () Direct channel (shipped): weighted-MLE lognormal literature ratio anchors (Smith 2026 medRxiv, Nelson 2009 paired, Kaper 1995, Harris 2012, Chao 2011, Finger 2018, Righetto 2012, Sugimoto 2014, MOSAIC calibration). (B) Derived channel: paired Monte-Carlo lognormal fitted \(\zeta_1\) / \(\zeta_2\) marginals, paired-bootstrap step shared Nelson 2009 anchor. (C) Combined: precision-weighted (inverse-variance) lognormal combination () (B). Diagnostic since 2026-04-23 (returned $diagnostics$fit_combined): median (~2e5) driven stool-concentration anchors overestimates ratio relative household-transmission modelling-convention evidence (Smith 2026 ~1.6x, Chao 2011 / Finger 2018 ~10). Direct channel (). Weighted MLE log10 literature ratio anchors direct-ratio table. anchors span ~1.6x (Smith 2026 household per-person-day) ~10^5 (Nelson 2009 paired stool concentrations). spread reflects genuinely different quantities (household transmission probability vs stool concentration ratio) preserved fit's sdlog. Derived channel (B). \(\zeta_1 \sim \mathrm{LN}(\mu_1, \sigma_1^2)\) \(\zeta_2 \sim \mathrm{LN}(\mu_2, \sigma_2^2)\) independent, ratio exactly \(\mathrm{LN}(\mu_1 - \mu_2, \sigma_1^2 + \sigma_2^2)\). derived channel uses analytic closed form directly. Nelson 2009 shared primary source marginals, principle induce positive correlation reduce ratio's variance, correctly propagating requires decomposing marginal's variance Nelson-attributable component residual independent component – subjective attribution well-supported available literature. closed-form variance \(\sigma_1^2 + \sigma_2^2\) therefore conservative upper bound true derived-channel spread. 100,000-draw Monte Carlo sample ratio distribution generated diagnostic figure returned $diagnostics$ratio_sample; enter fit statistics. Truncation 1. direct channel wide (anchors span ~1.6x ~10^5), untruncated lognormal puts non-trivial share mass 1 ($fit$p_below_1, 0.16 v0.100.0 anchors), inherited Smith 2026 household odds-ratio interval (0.11-3.23). draws give \(\zeta_2 > \zeta_1\), contradicts shedding biology model encodes: symptomatic stool carries \(10^5\)-\(10^8\) cells/mL litres per day (est_zeta_1_prior() anchors), asymptomatic carriers shed \(10^3\) (Nelson 2009) \(10^5\) (Kaper 1995) cells per gram formed stool (est_zeta_2_prior() anchors), model description samples ratio precisely rule \(\zeta_1 < \zeta_2\). Smith 2026 interval concerns household transmission odds, per-day shedding, license ratios 1. shipped prior therefore direct-channel lognormal truncated 1 (lower = 1): meanlog/sdlog unchanged removed mass redistributed proportionally \(\zeta_{\mathrm{ratio}} \ge 1\), moves median ($fit$median). Combined channel (C). Given direct derived fits \(\mathrm{LN}(\mu_A, \sigma_A^2)\) \(\mathrm{LN}(\mu_B, \sigma_B^2)\), precision-weighted mean log scale $$\mu_C = \frac{\mu_A / \sigma_A^2 + \mu_B / \sigma_B^2}{1/\sigma_A^2 + 1/\sigma_B^2}, \quad \sigma_C = \left(1/\sigma_A^2 + 1/\sigma_B^2\right)^{-1/2}$$ Bayesian posterior log-ratio flat priors channels treated independent normal likelihoods. Smith 2026 dose-response note. Smith et al. 2026 (medRxiv) report odds ratio 0.60 (95 percent CI 0.11-3.23) household transmission asymptomatic vs symptomatic index cases, giving inverse transmission ratio ~1.6. near-linear Hill dose-response regime equal contact patterns compatible low per-person-per-day zeta_ratio. value included weight 0.5 alongside Nelson's 10^5 stool-concentration ratio reader can see tension. fitdistrplus dependency. function import fitdistrplus. diagnostic_candidate_fits = TRUE package loaded via requireNamespace() graceful fallback; follows pattern R/est_initial_R.R:704-710.

what: Estimate Beta Prior for Rho (Care-Seeking Rate) and Save Parameter Data Frame — get_rho_care_seeking_params
title: Estimate Beta Prior for Rho (Care-Seeking Rate) and Save Parameter Data Frame — get_rho_care_seeking_params
text: pool two Wiens strata? Symptomatic cholera MOSAIC's setting spans full severity spectrum (mild watery diarrhea severe rapid dehydration). two Wiens 2025 meta-analytic strata bracket spectrum: General diarrhea (3+ loose/liquid stools): 29.9% (95% CI [25.3, 35.1]) 122 observations. Represents care-seeking broader population diarrheal episodes, appropriate mild--moderate tail symptomatic cholera (majority cases count). Severe diarrhea + cholera: 58.6% (95% CI [39.9, 75.2]) 22 observations. Represents care-seeking symptoms severe enough flagged "severe" specifically cholera, appropriate severe tail symptomatic cholera. Anchoring severe+cholera stratum ALONE biases rho upward (represents severe tail dominated outbreak-response settings enhanced care-seeking, e.g. Haiti 2010-19 outbreak contributes 50% underlying rows). Anchoring general diarrhea ALONE biases rho downward (broader category includes many mild, self-resolving episodes reflect cholera-specific severity). Random-effects pooling two strata produces estimate honestly reflects severity spectrum substantial heterogeneity. include GEMS Nasrin 2013 separate co-anchor? Earlier versions (v0.32.5) pooled GEMS pediatric moderate--severe diarrhea (4 SSA sites, 12 stratum-level estimates) Wiens severe+cholera pooled estimate. pooling three problems: (1) GEMS measures pediatric MSD care-seeking, different population MOSAIC's -ages cholera; (2) 12 GEMS strata vs. 1 Wiens meta-analytic summary upside-dimensionally; (3) Wiens 2025 already includes GEMS-derived data (6 Study IDs tagged GEMS/HUAS), direct GEMS entries partially double-counted source populations. Dropping GEMS using Wiens's two strata directly resolves three. Methodology. Random-effects meta-analysis logit scale (DerSimonian-Laird tau^2) two Wiens strata unit pooling. 95% CI pooled mean fit Beta distribution via get_beta_params. Geographic provenance (severe+cholera stratum). 23 underlying studies: 16 SSA, 3 Latin America/Caribbean (mostly Haiti 2010-19), 2 Bangladesh, 1 MENA, 1 South Asia (non-BGD). Predominantly SSA + outbreak settings - regime MOSAIC calibrates.

text: separate GAM (folded flood label). Tropical cyclones carry opposite climate signature ordinary precipitation floods: sharp wind spike short, crisply-dated footprint. flood-EM-DAT filter historically dropped 49 tropical-cyclone / surge events, neutered flood GAM's wind smooth. Modeling cyclones wind-led GAM restores signal clean input channel; psi LSTM recombines flood cyclone probabilities downstream (shared cholera-contamination mechanism lives LSTM, label). GAM fit mgcv::bam(), family = stats::binomial(link = "logit") (predictions naturally [0, 1]), method = "fREML", select = TRUE (smoothness null-space shrinkage – drives uninformative smooths toward zero, principled mechanism used impute_flood_probability). Predictors computed inline (caller need supply ): ENSO34 IOD lags 8, 16, 24 weeks (seasonal cyclone-season steering; SWIO cyclone activity co-varies ENSO/IOD phase). Nothing else – wind short-window precip channels acute proxy; country random effect absorbs baseline coastal-exposure differences. active fraction low (~74 weeks ~35k country-weeks, ~0.2%). country random effect s(iso_code_f, bs = "re") concentrates predicted probability historically cyclone-exposed coastal countries (MOZ, MWI, ZWE, MDG-adjacent belt) keeps landlocked / non-cyclone countries near zero. region-conditional wind smooth (s(wind_speed_10m_max, = region_f)) lets Southern Africa (cyclone belt) map wind risk steeply subregions. Sentinel handling mirrors flood imputer: NA prediction (lag warm-edge, residual missing predictor) filled country's mean predicted probability; global mean last resort. function asserts final column numeric, [0, 1], NA-free. diagnostics = TRUE, rolling-year CV (3 -recent fully-observed years) writes per-fold AUC / Brier / log-loss cyclone_gam_cv_metrics.csv. mean CV AUC 0.65 emits warning column still returned.

title: Impute Country-Week Drought Probability from a SPEI-Deficit Label — impute_drought_probability
text: Label (derived , EM-DAT events). EM-DAT drought records unusable weekly label (median ~344-day duration, dozens multi-year events, ~18/40 countries "active" single week – constant background wash). Instead label built panel's spei_approx (per-country standardized precipitation minus evapotranspiration): country-week drought_active = 1 12-week rolling mean spei_approx spei_threshold (default -0.8). 12-week window enforces "sustained" requirement (single dry week qualify) rolling mean standard meteorological way distinguish drought spell short-term dryness. production panel yields ~15% positive weeks across 38 countries recovers known meteorological droughts (Southern Africa 2015-16 El Nino & 2018-19, Horn Africa 2016-17, 2023-24 El Nino) – smeared multi-year mess EM-DAT drought type produces. CRITICAL leakage control. concurrent spei_approx label source, (rolling mean) excluded predictor set – predicting label generator trivially circular defeat entire purpose (lead-time mapping). applies local-climate series overlaps label's sustain_weeks window (precipitation temperature ingredients spei_approx), every local-climate predictor lagged sustain_weeks weeks: describes conditions strictly label window. predictors exogenous ocean-state teleconnections genuinely antecedent temperature / precipitation . GAM fit mgcv::bam(), family = stats::binomial(link = "logit"), method = "fREML", select = TRUE (smoothness null-space shrinkage). Predictors: ENSO34 IOD lags 8, 16, 24 weeks (slow ocean-state drivers LEAD drought season two – lead time product GAM sells LSTM). Antecedent temp_anom (heat amplifies evaporative demand), precip_anom, long-window antecedent precipitation precip_sum_12w / precip_sum_24w (accumulated rainfall deficit; 24w computed inline), lagged sustain_weeks ends week label window begins. s(iso_code_f, bs = "re") country random effect (baseline aridity / drought propensity). concurrent spei_approx rolling mean predictors (label leakage; see leakage-control note ). Fit rows limited date <= climate_obs_stop (<= gam_train_stop set). warning raised bam() reports non-convergence. output returned input's row order, whatever order . Slow integrator. Drought persistent state whose cholera relevance accumulates (WASH strain, water-source concentration, migration). single per-week probability -represents memory, trailing integrator_weeks-week mean probability emitted alongside. 26 weeks (~half year) chosen spans full dry-season build without bleeding prior year's drought next – long enough genuine slow channel, short enough remain seasonally resolved. backward-looking rolling mean (future leakage) warm-NAs filled country mean. Sentinel handling mirrors flood/cyclone imputers: NA predictions filled country mean, global mean. output columns asserted numeric, [0, 1], NA-free.

title: Impute Country-Week Flood Probability from EM-DAT and Climate Covariates — impute_flood_probability
text: four "enriched" predictors (added v0.30.23 prior v0.30.20-21 baseline) – long-memory antecedent precipitation 24-week 52-week horizons, region-conditional medium-window precip smooth, precip-anomaly x soil-moisture-anomaly joint interaction – improve detection major cyclone-driven flood events (Idai 2019, Kenneth 2019, Eloise 2021, Ana 2022, Gombe 2022, Freddy 2023). 10-cyclone benchmark formulation lands every event top 21% country's historical predicted-probability distribution (median 93rd percentile), reliable cyclone detector across rebuild strategies tested. GAM fit mgcv::bam() (mgcv's big-data variant – uses block updates, discrete covariate binning, parallel-friendly linear algebra; ~30k rows returns ~30-40 sec). family = stats::binomial(link = "logit") produces predictions naturally [0, 1] without rescaling. method = "fREML", select = TRUE (smoothness null-space shrinkage, principled mgcv mechanism driving uninformative smooths toward zero – replaces iterative -sample-p-value pruning loop v0.30.24 used). Predictors computed inline (caller need provide ): ENSO34 IOD lags 8, 16, 24 weeks (current value raw column). Long-memory antecedent precipitation: precip_sum_24w (~6-month basin saturation memory) precip_sum_52w (annual). Joint climate index: precip_anom * soil_moisture_anom (-wet already-saturated regime). Region-conditional precip-sum-4w smooth requires region column input dataframe (4-region classification: Central / East / Southern / West Africa). Sentinel handling: row whose prediction NA (e.g. lag-startup edge week 20 earliest year, row missing predictor survived upstream imputation) filled country's mean predicted probability. Rows even country mean NA fall back global mean. function asserts final column [0, 1] contains NAs. diagnostics = TRUE, function additionally runs rolling-year cross-validation: 3 recent fully-observed years Y, GAM refit rows year < Y used predict rows year == Y. Per-fold AUC, Brier score, log-loss written flood_gam_cv_metrics.csv. mean CV AUC 0.65, warning emitted function still returns column.

title: Create a Reusable MOSAIC Parallel Cluster — make_mosaic_cluster
text: n_cores Integer. Number worker processes (default: parallel::detectCores() - 1). Clamped number free R connections smaller, message – see Details. type Character. Cluster type: "PSOCK" (default, platforms) "FORK" (Linux/Mac , faster startup). require_root Logical. TRUE (default) root directory must set propagated workers, simulation workers need resolve get_paths(). FALSE allows cluster without one, workers handed explicit paths – render_MOSAIC_figures runs post-hoc finished run directory may MOSAIC tree .

title: Create a Reusable MOSAIC Parallel Cluster — make_mosaic_cluster
text: cluster object (parallel::makeCluster) ready pass run_MOSAIC(cluster = cl).

title: Create a Reusable MOSAIC Parallel Cluster — make_mosaic_cluster
text: cluster setup includes: Thread environment variables (OMP_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, TBB_NUM_THREADS, NUMBA_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS) set 1 main process worker prevent oversubscription. BLAS threads limited 1 per worker via .mosaic_set_blas_threads(1L). Libraries loaded worker: MOSAIC, arrow. Root directory propagated main process via set_root_directory(). Connection cap. worker holds one R connection. default R build permits 128 connections total, three already taken stdin, stdout stderr, requesting ~126 workers fails inside parallel::makeCluster(). n_cores therefore clamped parallelly::freeConnections() - 2 (two held back worker parquet /O) message reports clamp. R 4.4.0 later accept --max-connections=N 4096 raise ceiling. caller responsible stopping cluster done: parallel::stopCluster(cl). returned object also carries "mosaic_worker_pids" attribute recorded creation, run_MOSAIC() uses reap worker survives stopCluster() – see ?.mosaic_stop_cluster.

title: Create a Reusable MOSAIC Parallel Cluster — make_mosaic_cluster

title: Build the daily reported-CFR matrix mu_jt from annual estimates — make_mu_jt
text: Days past last estimated year carry year's value forward, simulation window runs beyond annual record filled recent estimate rather extrapolated trend. values GAM's logit-scale centres, .e. median year's reported-CFR distribution, mean. exact prior centre integrated deaths likelihood (whose year deviations mean zero logit scale). simulation draws deaths directly mu_jt – scenario run prior-predictive check – runs 5-10% -annual deaths (2018-25); logit-normal mean -predict, annual CFR lower high-case years. default "linear_logit" centre integrated likelihood's year deviations use different time bases purpose. deviations calendar-year levels blended 30 days either side 1 January (.d7_basis() calc_log_likelihood_deaths_integrated.R), centre interpolates 1 July anchors, January June centre sits partway toward previous year's value. resulting offset year--year change GAM centre (0.07 logit, 3 percent CFR, 2022-26 estimates) absorbed year deviation; years past last estimate held flat, forecast windows unaffected.

Names must match location_name. proportion fields provided analysis convenience required transmission model. prop_E_initial Optional. named numeric vector length equal location_name giving starting proportion exposed individuals location. Values must [0,1]. Names must match location_name. prop_I_initial Optional. named numeric vector length equal location_name giving starting proportion infected individuals location. Values must [0,1]. Names must match location_name. prop_V1_initial Optional. named numeric vector length equal location_name giving starting proportion individuals vaccine compartment V1 location. Values must [0,1]. Names must match location_name. prop_V2_initial Optional. named numeric vector length equal location_name giving starting proportion individuals vaccine compartment V2 location. Values must [0,1]. Names must match location_name. b_jt matrix birth rates rows equal length(location_name) columns equal daily sequence date_start date_stop. d_jt matrix mortality rates rows equal length(location_name) columns equal daily sequence date_start date_stop. nu_1_jt matrix first-dose OCV vaccinations location time step. nu_2_jt matrix second-dose OCV vaccinations location time step. phi_1 Effectiveness one dose OCV (numeric [0, 1]). phi_2 Effectiveness two doses OCV (numeric [0, 1]). omega_1 Waning immunity rate one dose (numeric >= 0). omega_2 Waning immunity rate two doses (numeric >= 0). nu_jt_sources Character vector compartment names eligible first-dose vaccination (default c("S", "E", "Isym", "Iasym", "R")). Must non-empty subset c("S", "E", "Isym", "Iasym", "R"). Passed laser-cholera v0.12+ draws first doses proportionally listed compartments. iota Incubation rate E -> (numeric > 0, per day). Note rate, period – prior median ~0.71/day. engine uses iota * E flow E. gamma_1 Symptomatic shedding-duration rate I_sym -> R (numeric, >= 0, per day; "severe / symptomatic" branch). gamma_2 Asymptomatic shedding-duration rate I_asym -> R (numeric, >= 0, per day; "mild / asymptomatic" branch). epsilon Natural-infection immunity waning rate R -> S (numeric, >= 0, per day). Distinct vaccine waning (omega_1, omega_2). mu_jt Reported case fatality ratio (reported deaths per reported suspected case) location day: matrix rows equal length(location_name) columns equal daily sequence date_start date_stop, per-location vector (constant time) scalar. Values [0, 1). returned config always carries full matrix. engine converts tick probability new symptomatic onset fatal, mu_jt * rho / (rho_deaths * chi_epidemic), reported deaths reported cases equal mu_jt epidemic-PPV ticks. endemic-PPV ticks reported CFR mu_jt * chi_endemic / chi_epidemic, endemic-dominated location calibrated mu_jt (true deaths ) can exceed observed CFR chi_epidemic / chi_endemic. Build annual data est_CFR_hierarchical() make_mu_jt(). mu_j_baseline Removed v0.96.0. pre-v0.96.0 baseline daily mortality hazard. Supplying marks input config written retired mortality model, whose mu_jt field never read engine, call refused rather silently reinterpreting matrix. Retained signature refusal names problem. mu_j_slope Deprecated ignored. linear--time mortality trend (1 + mu_j_slope * tick/nticks) removed engine v0.95.0 (CFR restructure R3): estimable deaths series, double-counted s(year) term already inside CFR_target, secular trend cholera CFR documented. Retained existing calls pass mu_j_slope explicitly fail unused-argument error; value supplied silently dropped returned config. mu_j_epidemic_factor Removed v0.96.0. pre-v0.96.0 epidemic mortality multiplier; treated exactly like mu_j_baseline. rho Care-seeking rate: probability symptomatic individual presents surveillance (numeric [0, 1]). reporting fraction sigma – upstream care-seeking step surveillance cascade. rho_deaths Death detection rate: probability true cholera death captured surveillance (numeric (0, 1]). engine thins true deaths produce reported_deaths, divides converting reported CFR mu_jt per-onset fatality probability, sets true deaths without moving reported deaths. sigma Proportion infections symptomatic (numeric [0, 1]). chi_endemic Positive predictive value among suspected cases endemic periods (numeric (0, 1]). chi_epidemic Positive predictive value among suspected cases epidemic periods (numeric (0, 1]). epidemic_threshold Isym/N point prevalence threshold switches case-reporting PPV chi_endemic chi_epidemic. Numeric scalar length-n vector [0, 1]. delta_reporting_cases Symptom-onset--surveillance reporting delay days (non-negative integer). infection--report – incubation handled separately E compartment iota. delta_reporting_deaths Deprecated ignored. Since v0.96.0 death reported lag case (delta_reporting_cases), surveillance record scored . Retained older configs still load; value supplied dropped returned. longitude numeric vector longitudes location. Must length location_name. latitude numeric vector latitudes location. Must length location_name. mobility_omega Exponent weight destination population gravity mobility model. Must numeric non-negative. mobility_gamma Exponent weight distance decay gravity mobility model. Must numeric non-negative. tau_i Departure probability origin location (numeric vector length(location_name) [0, 1]). beta_j0_tot Total baseline transmission rate (human + environmental). Optional numeric vector length(location_name). provided p_beta, used derive beta_j0_hum beta_j0_env. p_beta Proportion total transmission human--human (0-1). Optional numeric vector length(location_name). provided beta_j0_tot, used derive beta_j0_hum beta_j0_env. beta_j0_hum Baseline human--human transmission rate (numeric vector length(location_name)). beta_j0_tot p_beta provided, validated beta_j0_tot * p_beta. a_1_j Vector sine amplitude coefficients (1st harmonic) location. Numeric, length = length(location_name). a_2_j Vector sine amplitude coefficients (2nd harmonic) location. Numeric, length = length(location_name). b_1_j Vector cosine amplitude coefficients (1st harmonic) location. Numeric, length = length(location_name). b_2_j Vector cosine amplitude coefficients (2nd harmonic) location. Numeric, length = length(location_name). p Period seasonal forcing function. Scalar numeric > 0. Default 365 daily annual seasonality. alpha_1 FOI mixing exponent applied infectious term (/N) (numeric (0, 1]; 1 = well-mixed contacts). Dual-mode (laser-cholera v0.16.0+): scalar applied uniformly across patches, per-location vector length length(location_name). alpha_2 Exponent N_jt FOI denominator (numeric [0, 1]). alpha_2 = 1 frequency-dependent transmission (FOI proportional /N); alpha_2 = 0 density-dependent (FOI proportional ). single global scalar: engine rejects per-location vector. beta_j0_env Baseline environment--human transmission rate (numeric vector length(location_name)). beta_j0_tot p_beta provided, validated beta_j0_tot * (1 - p_beta). theta_j Proportion adequate WASH (numeric vector length(location_name) [0, 1]). psi_jt Matrix environmental suitability values (matrix rows = length(location_name) columns equal daily sequence date_start date_stop). psi_star_a Shape/gain parameter logit calibration psi_jt (numeric vector length(location_name) > 0). Values > 1 sharpen peaks, values < 1 flatten peaks. Default 1.0 (transformation). psi_star_b Scale/offset parameter logit calibration psi_jt (numeric vector length(location_name)). Shifts baseline /logit scale. Default 0.0 (offset). psi_star_z Smoothing weight causal EWMA calibrated psi_jt (numeric vector length(location_name) (0,1]). 1.0 = smoothing, < 1.0 = apply smoothing. Default 1.0 (smoothing). psi_star_k Time offset days psi_jt calibration (numeric vector length(location_name)). Positive values = forward/delay, negative values = backward/advance. Default 0.0 (offset). zeta_1 Shedding rate (numeric > 0). zeta_2 Asymptomatic shedding rate (numeric > 0). Derived sample_parameters() zeta_1 / zeta_ratio. kappa Concentration required 50% infection (numeric > 0). decay_days_short Time constant (days) short-term survival V. cholerae environment. Must > 0 < decay_days_long. decay_days_long Time constant (days) long-term survival V. cholerae environment. Must > 0 > decay_days_short. decay_shape_1 First shape parameter beta distribution controlling environmental suitability maps decay rate V. cholerae environment. Must numeric > 0. decay_shape_2 Second shape parameter beta distribution controlling environmental suitability maps decay rate V. cholerae environment. Must numeric > 0. reported_cases Matrix daily reported cholera cases. Must integer. NA allowed. nrow=length(location_name), ncol=length(t). reported_deaths Matrix daily reported cholera deaths. Must integer. NA allowed. nrow=length(location_name), ncol=length(t). epidemic_peaks Optional data.frame observed epidemic peaks consumed peak-timing / peak-magnitude shape terms calc_model_likelihood() (R Python port laser-cholera). Must contain two character columns: iso_code (matching entries location_name) peak_date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD strings parseable .Date). NULL allowed; NULL peak shape terms contribute 0 likelihood. sigfigs Ignored; retained backward compatibility. rounding applied, supplying raises warning.

what: Build Complete MOSAIC Control Structure — mosaic_control_defaults
title: Build Complete MOSAIC Control Structure — mosaic_control_defaults
text: Creates complete control structure run_mosaic(). primary interface configuring MOSAIC execution settings, consolidating calibration strategy, parameter sampling, parallelization, output options. Parameters organized workflow order: calibration: run (simulations, iterations, batch sizes) sampling: sample (parameters vary) likelihood: score model fit (likelihood components weights) targets: stop (ESS convergence thresholds) parallel: Infrastructure (cores, cluster type) io: Output format (file format, compression) paths: File management (output directories, plots)

title: Build Complete MOSAIC Control Structure — mosaic_control_defaults
code: mosaic_control_defaults(   calibration = NULL,   sampling = NULL,   likelihood = NULL,   targets = NULL,   predictions = NULL,   weights = NULL,   parallel = NULL,   io = NULL,   paths = NULL,   logging = NULL )

title: Build Complete MOSAIC Control Structure — mosaic_control_defaults
text: calibration List calibration settings. Default : n_simulations: NULL auto mode, integer fixed mode n_iterations: Number stochastic engine iterations per parameter set (default: 3L) max_simulations_total: Maximum total simulations across phases (default: 100000L) batch_size_adaptive: Simulations per batch Phase 1 adaptive calibration (default: 500L) min_batches_adaptive: Minimum Phase 1 batches convergence check (default: 5L) max_batches_adaptive: Maximum Phase 1 batches (default: 8L) max_batch_predictive: Cap Phase 2 predictive batch (default: 10000L) max_batches_predictive: Maximum Phase 2 predictive batches (default: 10L) target_r2_adaptive: ESS regression R-squared target Phase 1 convergence (default: 0.90) sampling List parameter sampling flags (sample). Default : sample_tau_i: Sample daily departure (travel) probability location (default: TRUE) sample_mobility_gamma: Sample gravity-model distance-decay exponent (default: TRUE) sample_mobility_omega: Sample gravity-model population-scaling exponent (default: TRUE) sample_iota: Sample incubation rate, E (default: TRUE) sample_gamma_2: Sample asymptomatic recovery rate (default: TRUE; second-dose vaccine effectiveness sample_phi_2) sample_alpha_1: Sample within-metapop population mixing exponent (default: FALSE, PINNED) sample_alpha_2: Sample frequency-dependence degree (default: FALSE; pinned, weakly identified) ... (see mosaic_control_defaults() complete list 40 flags) likelihood List likelihood calculation settings (score model fit). Default : weight_cases: Weight cases vs deaths (default: 1.0) weight_deaths: Weight deaths vs cases (default: 1.0) weight_wis: WIS regularizer weight (default: 0, ). 0.10 suggested v0.101.0 tuned daily cases core, default; weekly core (cases_scoring = "weekly") given weight weighs several times (median 4.8 times, range 1.8 6.5, v0.100.1 national re-selection pools; cases dispersion small), 0.02 keeps balance . re-tuned since; check fit relying cases_scoring: "daily" (default; one NB cell per day weekly k, cell rule v0.100.1 earlier) "weekly" (cases scored NB reporting-week totals). daily rule default weekly rule fitted cases worse v0.101.0 likelihood gate. Either rule runs dispersion version estimates, default reproduce v0.100.1 run: cases fit estimate , clamped lower bound, now takes panel trend, config reported_tier restricts cases k deaths dispersion observed weeks, ensemble intervals observation-level (weekly NB scored k either rule) cases central line median. Matching v0.100.1 likelihood also needs run's nb_k_cases (nb_dispersion.csv) config without reported_tier; resume refuses pool v0.100.1 simulations either way ... (see mosaic_control_defaults() complete list) targets List convergence targets (stop). Default : ESS_param: Target ESS per parameter (default: 100) ESS_param_prop: Proportion parameters meeting ESS (default: 0.95) ESS_best: Target subset size ESS within subset (default: 100). A_best: Target agreement index (default: 0.70). Lower values allow top sims dominate. CVw_best: Target CV weights (default: 1.0). Higher values permit sharper discrimination. min_best_subset: Smallest best-subset size searched (default: 30) max_best_subset: Largest best-subset size searched (default: 1000) ESS_method: ESS calculation method, "kish" "perplexity" (default: "perplexity") ESS_marginal_method: Per-parameter marginal ESS method, "kde" "binned" (default: "kde") best_subset_weighting: Best-subset posterior weights, "saturated" "tempered" (default: "saturated"; "tempered" sharper, softer) predictions List prediction generation settings. Default : n_iter_ensemble: Stochastic runs per posterior parameter set weighted ensemble (default: 10L). Total ensemble sims = N parameter sets x n_iter_ensemble. n_iter_best: Stochastic runs medoid single-config prediction plots (default: 100L). Applied identically models. runs execute internal PSOCK cluster parallel$enable = TRUE. optimize_subset: Logical; TRUE, post-ensemble optimizer (MAE / WIS / R^2+bias) refines best subset used posteriors.json, posterior_quantiles.csv, ensemble object driving downstream plots metrics. tier-selected subset preserved is_best_subset / weight_best columns samples.parquet provenance; optimized selection written new is_best_subset_opt / weight_best_opt columns. FALSE (default), tier-selected subset canonical _opt columns written. Statistical note: enabling flag yields posterior conditioned ensemble predictive performance (MAE / WIS / R^2+bias training data) rather pure likelihood-weighted posterior. optimize_min_n: Minimum subset size optimizer may select (default 30L, raised 4L guard KDE degeneracy posteriors.json). optimize_objective: Objective function, "mae" (default), "r2_bias", "wis". optimize_stride: Integer >= 1 (default 3L). 1L evaluates every candidate subset size min_n:max_n (exhaustive, bit-identical historical search). > 1L runs coarse--refine search evaluates strided grid first refines around best point. default 3L gives roughly 3x speedup negligible accuracy cost smooth score(N) curve (re-examines +/- 3 window around coarse winner); raise (5L/10L/25L) speed, set 1L force exhaustive search. Note may select slightly different optimal_n exhaustive records evaluated N's diagnostics table. (optimize_ensemble_subset function's stride default remains 1L preserve bit-identicality.) central_method: Ensemble central tendency, "mean" (expected count, never collapses zero sparse deaths) "median" (typical trajectory, robust explosive members). Scalar per-channel c(cases=, deaths=); default c(cases = "median", deaths = "mean") since v0.101.0 (mean v0.98.0 v0.100.x, median v0.46.1 v0.97.x). Either way line summary engine-level member trajectories; intervals observation-level. Governs prediction trajectory + plots, canonical *_ensemble R^2/bias metrics, medoid target, subset-selection objective consistently. number parameter sets ensemble determined best subset (sims non-zero importance weights). weights List importance-weight settings. Default : floor: Minimum weight prevent underflow (default: 1e-15). iqr_multiplier: Tukey IQR outlier-detection multiplier (default: 1.5; use 3.0 extreme outliers ). parallel List parallelization settings (infrastructure). Default : enable: Enable parallel execution (default: FALSE) n_cores: Number simulation worker processes (default: 1L) type: Cluster type, "PSOCK" "FORK" (default: "PSOCK") progress: Show progress bar (default: TRUE) io List /O settings (output format). Default : format: Output format; "parquet" supported ("csv" coerced "parquet" warning) compression: Compression algorithm (default: "zstd") compression_level: Compression level (default: 3L) persist_ensemble_arrays: Retain dense 4-D arrays – observation-level cases_array/deaths_array engine-level cases_engine_array/deaths_engine_array – persisted ensemble RDS files (ensemble_candidate.rds, ensemble_optimized.rds, subset_opt.rds, medoid_ensemble.rds). Default FALSE strips arrays save time -disk artifacts small (~tens KB); every light field (central tendencies, envelopes, weights, seeds, obs, metadata) preserved standard consumers (plotting, OCV, rolling CV) work unchanged. Set TRUE re-analysable raw archive (e.g. re-running subset optimization R_eff posterior-resimulation CI path saved file). -memory object used run never affected (default: FALSE). paths List path output settings (file management). Default : clean_output: Remove output directory exists (default: FALSE) plots: Generate diagnostic plots (default: TRUE) logging List logging settings. Default : verbose: Enable detailed progress messages sub-functions (default: FALSE).

title: Build Complete MOSAIC Control Structure — mosaic_control_defaults
code: # Default control settings ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults()  # Quick parallel run with 8 cores ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   parallel = list(enable = TRUE, n_cores = 8) )  # Fixed mode with 5000 simulations, 5 iterations each ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   calibration = list(     n_simulations = 5000,     n_iterations = 5   ) )  # Auto mode with custom settings ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   calibration = list(     n_simulations = NULL,  # NULL = auto mode     n_iterations = 3,     max_simulations_total = 50000,     batch_size_adaptive = 1000   ),   parallel = list(enable = TRUE, n_cores = 16) )  # Only sample specific parameters ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   sampling = list(     sample_tau_i = TRUE,     sample_mobility_gamma = FALSE,     sample_mobility_omega = FALSE,     sample_beta_j0_tot = TRUE,     sample_iota = FALSE,     sample_gamma_2 = FALSE,     sample_alpha_1 = FALSE   ) )  # Enable WIS regularizer and peak timing ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   likelihood = list(     weight_wis = 0.02,     weight_peak_timing = 0.25   ) )  # Use perplexity method for ESS calculations ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   targets = list(ESS_method = "perplexity") )  # Full workflow configuration (demonstrates logical order) ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   calibration = list(n_simulations = NULL, n_iterations = 3),      # How to run   sampling = list(sample_tau_i = TRUE, sample_beta_j0_tot = TRUE),  # What to sample   likelihood = list(weight_wis = 0.02, weight_cases = 1.0),        # How to score   targets = list(ESS_param = 100, ESS_param_prop = 0.95),          # When to stop   parallel = list(enable = TRUE, n_cores = 16),                    # Infrastructure   io = mosaic_io_presets("default"),                               # Output format   paths = list(clean_output = FALSE, plots = TRUE)                 # File management )

Produces separate mosaic_ensemble object optimal subset size, leaving original ensemble untouched. candidate size N (min_n full ensemble), function re-computes best-subset weights within top-N subset, re-computes weighted median predictions 4D arrays, scores selected objective function. Selection scores ENGINE-level member trajectories (ensemble$cases_engine_array/deaths_engine_array; cases_array/deaths_array ensemble saved v0.101.0, engine-level), series ensemble's central lines built . optimized ensemble rebuilt exactly calc_model_ensemble builds one: central lines engine draws interval envelope predictive_median observation-level draws selected members, ensemble carries . "wis" objective therefore scores engine-level spread. per-N weights use scheme weight_best posterior run_MOSAIC() builds candidate ensemble (default \(w \propto \exp(-0.5 \min(\Delta, 4))\) \(\Delta = -2(\ell - \max \ell)\) within top N). Separately, ensemble$seeds present (per-member seeds carried calc_model_ensemble, aligned cases_array construction), carried sort/slice exposed ensemble_optimized$seeds cases_array-aligned consumers medoid selection. argument ensemble$seeds serve different roles kept independent. min_n Minimum subset size evaluate. Default 30L guard small-subset KDE degeneracy optimized subset drives posterior artifacts. Fox et al. (2024) report 4 statistical minimum accuracy, posterior density estimation needs larger N. objective Scoring function: "mae" (default, normalized MAE), "r2_bias" (R-squared plus bias penalty), "wis" (normalized Weighted Interval Score). central_method Central tendency used summarize per-cell ensemble distribution "mae" "r2_bias" objectives recorded R^2/bias/MAE diagnostics: "median" (default, reproduces historical selection) "mean" (weighted mean, unbiased expected counts). Scalar per-channel c(cases=, deaths=).
